tickets.title: Vocabularies as tenant settings: channel words, visit buckets, ladder order and depth (**in scope since amendment 1, 2026-10-09**)

authority.locator: P36 · Vocabularies as tenant settings, section E (amendment 1); the customer's T7 entry channel, source platform, landing-page type and visit number; the investigation §2.5, DI-1, DI-2, DI-6
authority.requirement: the entry-channel vocabulary (paid_social, paid_search_brand, paid_search_nonbrand, organic, email, sms, affiliate, referral, direct, the brand split from a published `utm_campaign` rule), the source platform (from the network list and a token-form `utm_source`), the landing-page type kept for the visit, the visit buckets and the ladder order and depth are per-tenant, versioned settings published without a deployment; the classification of UTM parameters and referrers into those values is a published mapping; an arrival whose evidence maps to no value records as unknown, never a guess; the page may pass its own channel only as a value of the tenant's vocabulary; a tenant without the settings keeps today's six words and classification exactly; a vocabulary change carries W25's grammar bump and prior re-export; the console shows and edits the settings; the kit states the vocabulary and the mapping.

tickets.outcome: The entry-channel vocabulary, its UTM and referrer classification, the source platform, the landing-page type, the visit buckets and the ladder order and depth are per-tenant versioned settings published without a deployment, so the customer's nine channels classify on both hosts, while a tenant without the settings keeps today's six words and classification exactly.

tickets.title: Device and recency as first-paint context

authority.locator: P37 · Device and recency as first-paint context, section E (amendment 1); the customer's T6 rows 3 and 5; the investigation §2.6, DI-3, DI-4
authority.requirement: the engine reads a device class at the edge from the request's client hints, else its user agent (mobile, desktop), and a recency bucket from the stored last visit (same day, within 7 days, 8 to 30 days, 30 and more; a first visit has none); both are seed-signal keys a seed rule can name; device is a P01 context term (an order may be published for a context that names a device beside, or instead of, a channel and a visit bucket; the most specific match wins; a context naming no device matches every device, so every receipted P01 order keeps its meaning) and a part of P30's context key; the receipt itemises device and recency when they decided anything; P07's aggregation is unchanged; a tenant publishing no device context and no recency rule behaves exactly as today; the kit documents both.

tickets.title: The published vocabulary as the authority for product and content attributes

authority.locator: P38 · The published vocabulary as the authority for product and content attributes, section E (amendment 1); the customer's T7 rules; the investigation §3.4, DI-9
authority.requirement: a vocabulary document lists every attribute (category, product type with its parent category, collection, style, colour, material, price band, price status, inventory status, bestseller status, occasion, gender, size, content format and imagery, content theme, journey-stage fit) with its values, each an id (lower case, words joined by underscores, at most 64 characters, none of the CSV tag separators), a display name that keeps the customer's wording and synonyms; the catalogue import and the event ingest map source values through one mapping table, resolving synonyms there, so data arriving already mapped passes through unchanged; a value outside the list is refused at publication and reported with the piece and the field; revisions are versioned and take effect only when approved; a tenant without a vocabulary keeps today's free-text behaviour exactly; the kit documents the schema and the mapping table.

tickets.outcome: A versioned, approved vocabulary document is the authority for product and content attribute values: imports and event ingest map source values through its mapping table, a value outside the list is refused at publication and reported with the piece and the field, and a tenant without a vocabulary keeps today's free-text behaviour exactly.

tickets.title: Module events as the customer defines them

authority.locator: P40 · Module events as the customer defines them, section E (amendment 1); the customer's T8 rows 1 to 14; the investigation §2.4, DI-13, DI-14, DI-15, DI-17
authority.requirement: the SDK records a viewable impression (at least 50 percent of the container in view for at least 1 second) beside the render acknowledgement, as a distinct event that weighs 0 and never builds interest, changing no denominator; `video_view` at 3 seconds is a content action that reads the piece's format from the catalogue, as `video_complete` does; a dwell minimum per slot (30 seconds on editorial) in the SDK, and `product_dwell` (20 seconds on a product page, once per view) accepted with `dwellMs`; purchase outcomes are unique per order id on the engine side; `search` (the resolved values, never the query text), `filter_applied` (the facet's dimension and value; the sale filter and the sale page raising `priceStatus: sale`), `product_dwell` and `remove_from_cart` (captured at weight 0 until P39) are documented in the kit as event conventions with their registry values; size guide and reviews opened are documented as declared interactions of the module that owns them (P03).

tickets.outcome: The SDK and both hosts record the customer's event definitions beside P03's receipted events: a viewable impression that changes no denominator, a video view at 3 seconds as a content action, a dwell minimum per slot and a product dwell, purchases unique per order id, and the kit's event conventions for search, filters, product dwell, remove from cart and declared interactions.

criteria.observable: The SDK sends one viewable impression per module per page instance, after the render acknowledgement, once at least half of the container has been in view for at least one second continuously, carrying the module identifier, the slot, the position within the slot and the decision identifier; a container shown less than half or less than one second sends none; on both hosts it weighs 0, builds no interest and changes no exposure count, so P03's units and the W26 exposure locks still pass.
criteria.proof: The P40 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P40.EV1 in src/units/P40 and they pass.

criteria.observable: On both hosts video_view at 3 seconds is a content action that reads the piece's format from the catalogue as video_complete does, at the tenant's weight (default 1), and the SDK offers it beside videoComplete.
criteria.proof: The P40 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P40.EV2 in src/units/P40 and they pass.

criteria.observable: The dwell minimum is configurable per slot in the SDK (the default of one second unchanged where none is configured), and product_dwell (once per product view, carrying dwellMs of at least 20 seconds) is accepted on both hosts and feeds the visit's dwell counter.
criteria.proof: The P40 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P40.EV3 in src/units/P40 and they pass.

criteria.observable: On both hosts a purchase is unique per order id for the shopper: a second purchase event carrying the same order id is recorded once, crediting once and building interest once, with the duplicate reported.
criteria.proof: The P40 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P40.EV4 in src/units/P40 and they pass.

criteria.observable: The kit documents the viewable impression, video_view, the dwell minimum, product_dwell, purchase uniqueness, and the event conventions search (the resolved values only, never the query text), filter_applied (the facet's dimension and value, the sale filter and the sale page raising priceStatus sale) and remove_from_cart (captured at weight 0 until P39), and the declared interactions sizeguide:open and reviews:open, in docs/kit/01-integration-guide.md, docs/kit/02-api-reference.md and docs/kit/03-payload-schemas.md.
criteria.proof: The P40 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P40.EV5 in src/units/P40 and they pass.

tickets.title: Negative preference with an expiry: remove from cart and the purchase rule

authority.locator: P39 · Negative preference with an expiry, section E (amendment 1); the customer's T8 row 15 and the purchase rule; the investigation DI-12, DI-16
authority.requirement: a named action (`remove_from_cart`) suppresses, for the shopper, the values it names for a configurable window; a server-confirmed purchase strengthens the product's style, collection, colour and price band at the purchase weight and suppresses the bought product type for a configurable window (default 30 days), after which the suppression lapses; a suppressed value does not lead a decision on the shopper's own interest while suppressed and context terms are unaffected; the receipt itemises each suppression with its expiry; the floor is unaffected (R-P33); a tenant without the settings behaves exactly as today; the kit documents the rule. Dismissal and other negative signals stay phase two.

tickets.outcome: A named action suppresses, for the shopper and for a configurable window, the values it names, and a server-confirmed purchase strengthens style, collection, colour and price band while suppressing the bought product type for a configurable window, itemised on the receipt and replayed exactly, with the floor unaffected and a tenant without the settings behaving exactly as today.

criteria.observable: A tenant publishes the suppression settings (the suppressing actions with each action's window in days; the purchase window in days) without a deployment, a window that is not a positive whole number of days is refused by name, and the action weights stay bounded 0 to 1000 as today.
criteria.proof: The P39 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P39.NP1 in src/units/P39 and they pass.

criteria.observable: On both hosts remove_from_cart carrying product values suppresses, for that shopper, the values it names for the action's window: the next decision does not lead with a piece on the shopper's own interest in a suppressed value while other values and every context term are unaffected; after the window the suppression lapses; and the shopper's count of signals is unchanged, because the action weighs 0.
criteria.proof: The P39 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P39.NP2 in src/units/P39 and they pass.

criteria.observable: On both hosts a server-confirmed purchase strengthens the product's style, collection, colour and price band at the purchase weight and suppresses the bought product type for the purchase window, and the complements preference still serves the matching piece on the page of the product it completes, as today.
criteria.proof: The P39 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P39.NP3 in src/units/P39 and they pass.

criteria.observable: The record and the receipt itemise each suppression in force with the value, the action and its expiry; a decision with a suppression replays exactly; a retained record without one replays as before.
criteria.proof: The P39 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P39.NP4 in src/units/P39 and they pass.

criteria.observable: A tenant without the settings decides term for term as today on both hosts, replay included, and every unit of src/units/P10 still passes.
criteria.proof: The P39 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P39.NP5 in src/units/P39 and they pass.

criteria.observable: The kit documents the suppression settings, the purchase rule and the receipt line in docs/kit/02-api-reference.md and docs/kit/03-payload-schemas.md.
criteria.proof: The P39 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P39.NP6 in src/units/P39 and they pass.

criteria.observable: Negative preference is per-shopper suppression with an expiry, never a negative weight.
criteria.proof: Decision D1.

criteria.observable: The windows and the action list are tenant settings with the lead's defaults: 30 days for the purchase rule and for remove from cart, full suppression.
criteria.proof: Decision D2.

criteria.observable: The released artifact shows the behaviour of every LOCAL criterion on both deployed shopper hosts.
criteria.proof: The LIVE1 walkthrough record.

criteria.observable: The customer's data science agrees the suppression windows and the action list, published as the tenant's settings before the rule is enabled.
criteria.proof: The LIVE2 agreement record.

existingEvidence.description: Every action weight is bounded 0 to 1000 at validation; a negative weight is refused.
The accumulation applies a weight above 0 only and floors interest at zero; nothing damps one dimension after a purchase.
The complements preference that serves the matching piece on the page of the product it completes.
The floor counts actions whose own weight is above zero; remove_from_cart at weight 0 is no signal.
The negative-preference options; the first, per-shopper suppression with an expiry, is the mechanism.

remainingWork: Type and validator: the suppression settings with their windows and the named refusals, the weight bound kept.
Shopper state: record a suppression per value with its expiry on both hosts in the shared reflex step, merge it on a link, lapse it after the window.
Decision path: exclude a suppressed value from leading on the shopper's own interest, context terms unaffected; regenerate public/meridian/engine.bundle.js.
Purchase rule: strengthen style, collection, colour and price band at the purchase weight and suppress the bought product type for the purchase window.
Receipt and replay: itemise each suppression with its expiry and replay it exactly.
Kit: document the settings, the rule and the receipt line in docs/kit/02-api-reference.md and docs/kit/03-payload-schemas.md.
